terms.gloss: pay one’s share of a shared meal
terms.comment: Lewis & Short s.v. symbola: “a contribution of money to a feast, a share of a reckoning, one’s scot”. The young men of comedy each pay their symbola towards a dinner; to dine so is dē symbolīs esse. In plain prose, “pay separately” is sēparātim solvere, and “pay together” ūnā solvere; where one pays for all, see “it’s on me”.

terms.gloss: dine on shared contributions, each paying a share
evidence: Ter. Eun. 540: ut dē symbolīs essēmu'

phrases.english: We’d like to pay separately, please.
“And what about Pamphilus?” “Pamphilus? He paid his share and had his dinner.”

phrases.latin: Herī aliquot adulēscentulī coiimus in Pīraeō in hunc diem, ut dē symbolīs essēmu'.
phrases.english: Yesterday a few of us young men got together at the Piraeus to arrange a dinner for today, each paying his share.

sources: Lewis & Short: symbola · Lewis & Short: separatim
